scope: Independent visual and scientific judgment frozen before reading any root-author verdict or generation receipt
positiveFindings: The two panels use the same generic, explicitly labelled rechargeable Akku as a suitable qualitative reversible-cell example: voluntary discharge to a lamp, externally forced charging by a charger.

The discharging battery has two separate wires. The red positive-terminal lead ends at the metal threaded shell of the bulb; the negative-terminal lead ends at the separate bottom contact. Neither lead ends in the glass and the drawing shows no short-circuit junction.
Charging connects charger plus to battery plus and charger minus to battery minus using two separate wires. No polarity swap or crossed wire is depicted.
Large yellow arrows are explicitly labelled Energie abgeben and Energie zuführen. Their directions represent energy transfer, not electron movement or conventional current.
Headings, positive/negative poles, charger, lamp, battery labels, energy labels and both limiting footer sentences are readable in the actual 360px view as well as at 680px.

The footer explicitly denies general rechargeability. The empty-battery phrase is an everyday statement about current inability to supply usable energy; in the adjacent charging context it does not imply chemical exhaustion, irreversible damage or equilibrium.

The imported altText accurately describes the actual objects, circuit polarity, energy directions and the qualitative model. Its currently-not-usable wording makes the situational meaning of leer explicit.
limits: No particular cell chemistry, redox half-equations, equilibrium state, charging parameters or safe practical charging procedure is specified. These are not certified by the orientation image.
Chemical reversal during discharge/charge of the suitable cell and the limits of everyday phrases still require explanation and learner evidence.
The generic charger has no external mains lead drawn; the labelled external charger is a qualitative energy source, not a complete electrical installation drawing.

A battery called empty may retain reactions or serve another smaller load. The footer is interpreted in the intended use context, and the altText says currently not usable; it is not a universal zero-energy assertion.
altText: Zwei Comic-Szenen zeigen denselben geeigneten Akku beim Entladen an einer Lampe und beim Laden an einem externen Ladegerät. Gelbe Energiepfeile zeigen beim freiwilligen Entladen vom Akku zur Lampe und beim erzwungenen Laden vom Ladegerät zum Akku. Getrennte Leitungen verbinden die Pole; am Ladegerät ist Plus mit Plus und Minus mit Minus verbunden. Große Hinweise begrenzen die Aussage: Nicht jede Batterie ist aufladbar; leer bedeutet aktuell nicht mehr nutzbar. Das qualitative Schema zeigt keine konkrete Zellchemie und behauptet kein chemisches Gleichgewicht oder allgemeine Umkehrbarkeit.
